claim: The pace limiter a game needs follows its structure: none where it waits on its own interrupts or HALTs, a fixed-stretch credit with no frame sync, a K window for a flat-out game.

evidence.text: A game waiting on its own interrupts needs no K window: 28 MHz to the wait is enough, fine windows only add cost.
Updates held by HALTs only need their time right at the frame edge; plots at 28 MHz need no window.
No frame sync and a hook cost per draw needs no limiter: run a fixed stretch of the same draw's set-up at 28 MHz.
A game with no frame wait needs a K window round all it can, or every hook entry at 3.5 MHz is its own cost.
A CPU-bound game can be paced by running one of its own long routines at 28 MHz; the build was +15% before.
